title: Confidence Interval Estimation
description: Quantifying estimation precision for population parameters using parametric formulas and empirical bootstrapping.
conditions: Reporting point estimates (mean, median, proportion, risk ratio, difference in means)
Need to communicate statistical uncertainty beyond single p-values
recommended_methods: Student's t-distribution confidence interval for normal means [Mean +/- t*(s/sqrt(n))]
Wilson Score interval for binomial proportions (superior to Wald normal approximation)
Non-parametric bootstrap percentile confidence interval (1,000+ resamples)
selection_rules: Always report 95% Confidence Intervals alongside point estimates in executive summaries
For proportions close to 0 or 1, never use Wald normal approximation (p +/- 1.96*SE); use Wilson Score
For medians, quantiles, or complex ratios, compute 95% BCa (bias-corrected and accelerated) bootstrap intervals
limitations: A 95% CI does not mean there is a 95% probability the true parameter lies in that specific interval (frequentist interpretation)
Bootstrap intervals require sufficient sample size (N >= 30) to adequately sample tail variation
source: Efron (1979) Bootstrap Methods: Another Look at the Jackknife
